quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use brakes. Instead, downshift.

questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes to slow down or stop safely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. You need extra time to notice when the vehicle stops and to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What can increase rider fatigue?

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.explanation: Dress properly to protect yourself from tiring weather like wind and rain. Limit rides to six hours per day and take a break every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants, as you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: How can you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve the bike toward the safest area.
Accelerate while keeping the brake on.

questions.explanation: To regain control of a locked rear wheel, release the brake. However, if the rear brake locks on a surface with good grip, you can keep it locked until the motorcycle stops completely.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change. Choose a position that gives you the most space and helps other drivers see you better.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of wobbling on your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to stop a wobble.

questions.question: When may you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: You need more following distance if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or in heavy traffic when another driver may cut in front of you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should stay just behind the leader, near the front of the group. This lets more experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best riding formation?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Move into a single-file line when turning, riding in curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When loading cargo onto a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle will affect your control.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of or in addition to turn signals. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the rider is turning right or changing lanes to the right.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, motorcyclists riding in a group should:

options.text: Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for groups. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When riding at night you should:

options.text: Use the headlights of the vehicle in front of you to see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of the vehicle in front of you to see ahead.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes when riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Stay flexible with your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: Which of the following will help you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, use both brakes, and avoid sudden moves. Stay away from the center of the lane and follow tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should not:

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges, as these are more slippery.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol is both illegal and unsafe.

questions.question: If you need to brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
Brake as hard as you would on a straightaway.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, it should be:

options.text: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Parked at a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Parked like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
Parked at the left edge of the parking space so drivers can see it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching the curb.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you see a police officer.
When another car is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another car is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light when someone is tailgating you. This warns the other driver that you are about to slow down. It also alerts them to hazards they may not see. Flashing your brake light is especially important before slowing down in places where drivers do not expect it.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group ride?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. More experienced riders can then watch them from behind and help keep them safe.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when the front brake is used.
Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is used.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes at the same time.
Remembers the braking force the rider usually uses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is used.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system automatically applies some front braking when you use the rear brake. This is a type of linked braking system. Read your motorcycle's owner's manual to learn more about your specific braking system.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulatory signs are rectangular. They are white with black lettering. You must obey the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. This hand signal means "follow me."
